messages:
incident-bot: Pager: SEV-2: API gateway reachability errors (TLS handshake failures) — paging oncall-sre @here

oncall-sre: Acked. I'm on it. tagging infra and obs.

alex.m: seeing lots of 525/526s from customers, and `curl` to api.redwood.ai times out at TLS handshake. reproducing from my workstation: `curl -v https://api.redwood.ai` shows `SSL: connection reset by peer`.

maria.p: Observability alert: spikes in edge latency and connection resets starting ~12:07 UTC, correlated with DNS errors from our resolver layer. Grafana: `edge.tls.handshake_failures` x8 baseline.

infra: I'm seeing a flood of SERVFAIL responses when resolving `api.redwood.ai` via 1.1.1.1 in us-west-2 and us-east-1. Query trace: ``
; <<>> DiG 9.11.3-1ubuntu1.15-Ubuntu <<>> @1.1.1.1 api.redwood.ai +trace
;; global options: +cmd
;; connection timed out; no servers could be reached
``

josh.k: Cloudflare status shows "partial outage - DNS resolver throttling affecting some regions" — https://status.cloudflare.com/incidents/xyz. Also seeing increased 5xxs in Cloudflare logs.

oncall-sre: Possible path: Cloudflare's resolver cluster returning SERVFAILs -> our API gateway can't establish TLS -> clients see handshake failures. Need to confirm whether it's DNS or edge routing. Maria, can you dump the edge eBPF metrics?

maria.p: Pasted snapshot to thread: `edge_dns_failure_rate` up 700% in us-west. Edge metrics show healthy pods locally but connection attempts to client IPs stall at `syn-ack` phase.

infra: Quick mitigation plan: 1) Fail over authoritative DNS from Cloudflare to secondary provider (Route53) by lowering TTL and updating glue. 2) Add explicit resolver fallback in our ingress to use 8.8.8.8 and our internal cache. 3) Shift traffic away from affected CF POPs using routing policy.

oncall-sre: Let's do 1 and 2 immediately. Who has Route53 creds?

josh.k: I have Route53 access. Lowering TTL on `api.redwood.ai` from 60s -> 10s now. Pushing new A/ALIAS records to point to our standby gateway: `aws route53 change-resource-record-sets --hosted-zone-id ZZZ --change-batch file://swap.json`

infra: Adding fallback resolvers to kube-proxy + envoy for gateway: `resolv_conf: nameserver 8.8.8.8` and restart envoy pods with zero-downtime rolling restart. Patching now.

alex.m: After switching resolver to 8.8.8.8 on one gateway, TLS handshake improved for ~30% of requests. Still some clients show intermittent errors (mobile carriers sometimes cache resolvers).

product-ops: Customer-impact update: Several customers in US and EU report degraded API calls (timeouts and TLS errors). Support tickets increasing. Marking customer communications as "investigating third-party DNS/CDN issue".

obs-bot: Alert: Synthetic check from eu-west-1 now passes intermittently. us-west-2 still ~40% failure.

maria.p: Deployed resolver fallback and route change. Observability shows handshake failures starting to trend down after 12:22 UTC. Still seeing spikes when requests route to specific CF POPs (iad/ord).

oncall-sre: Temporary mitigation effective but not fully healed. Next step: enforce Cloudflare POP exclusion for affected regions so traffic routes to other CDNs/peers. Also prepare an emergency rollback to Dedicated nodes in our Reserved pool (bypass CF) if failure persists.

josh.k: Initiating POP exclusion via Traffic Manager policy: `traffic-manager exclude-pop iad,ord` — change committed. Routing should propagate within ~60s.

infra: Also kicked off a support ticket with Cloudflare (ticket #CF-4521). They confirm a resolver cluster is overloaded and are throttling queries. They estimate fix ETA ~40 mins.

alex.m: Noted that some customers using long-lived TLS connections saw connection resets but could reconnect after DNS TTL expiry. For customers behind corporate proxies, issues may persist longer.

product-ops: Drafted status update for customers, will post to status.redwood.ai and notify top 10 enterprise customers. Keep me posted on ETA.

oncall-sre: Handoff: I'll be on incident for the next 45m then hand to next oncall. Current severity: SEV-2 (widespread degraded API reachability for regions). Active mitigations: Route53 failover, resolver fallback to 8.8.8.8, Cloudflare POP exclusion, contacting CF support.

josh.k: CF confirmed mitigation rollout to their resolvers; some relief seen. Still monitoring.

maria.p: Observability note — enable higher sample rate for TLS flows for 1h so we can capture client IPs + SNI for postmortem. Doing that now.

infra: Preparing postmortem checklist: timeline, root cause (third-party resolver throttling), mitigation timeline, follow-ups: 1) multi-resolver strategy in control plane 2) automated DNS failover playbook 3) update runbooks to include POP exclusion steps 4) test DNS failover quarterly.

product-ops: Customer comms posted at 12:35 UTC. Notifying affected enterprise contacts.

oncall-sre: We appear to be trending to healthy at 12:42 UTC. Monitoring for additional regressions. Will hand to next oncall at 13:00 UTC.

incident-bot: Note: On-call handover scheduled to @oncall-sre-next at 13:00 UTC.

alex.m: Thanks team. Logging the commands I ran for the postmortem: 
``
# quick DNS failover
aws route53 change-resource-record-sets --hosted-zone-id ZZZ --change-batch '{"Changes":[{"Action":"UPSERT","ResourceRecordSet":{"Name":"api.redwood.ai","Type":"A","TTL":10,"ResourceRecords":[{"Value":"3.12.45.67"}]}}]}'
# force envoy resolver to fallback
kubectl -n infra set env deploy/gateway RESOLVERS=8.8.8.8,1.1.1.1
kubectl -n infra rollout restart deploy/gateway
```

product-ops: Closing notes: severity will downgrade to SEV-3 after 1h of stable signal. We'll schedule a postmortem meeting tomorrow and include CF contact.

oncall-sre: Handoff complete. Logging incident and switching pager to @oncall-sre-next.

josh.k: Closing Cloudflare ticket if they confirm resolved. CF updated: resolved for affected resolver cluster at 12:58 UTC.

maria.p: Final note: Will open a follow-up for infra to implement multi-resolver + runbook tasks. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
